title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
content:
The Pentagon has launched versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok, giving 3 million civilian and military personnel access to generative AI tools that have been tailored to “warfighter needs.”
ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government — custom versions of the popular consumer generative AI tools — are now part of GenAI.mil, a centralized, secure portal launched last year.
GenAI.mil, which offered Google Gemini when it first launched, is designed to give Department of Defense employees access to commercial frontier AI models without sending sensitive government data through ordinary consumer channels. In particular, the official military version is exempt from the data collection that is difficult to avoid in consumer tech products.
And according to the Department of Defense, the generative AI portal has proven popular. GenAI.mil has already onboarded more than 1.7 million unique users out of the department’s 3 million personnel, according to the department.
These latest additions are part of the Pentagon’s broader effort to use AI tools to accelerate work and give the Department of Defense an edge without sacrificing security. They also highlight the absence of Anthropic’s Claude model and the Pentagon’s effort to work with other companies following its dispute with the frontier lab. Anthropic was labeled a supply-chain risk by the Trump administration — a designation that it is currently fighting in court — after it refused to give the Pentagon unrestricted use of its AI tools and instead insisted on certain safety guardrails.
ChatGPT Mil, which came out of the company’s OpenAI for Government program, will offer an experience familiar to commercial ChatGPT users. The tool will focus on chat, files, projects, and custom GPTs, according to the Defense Department. The tool will also support document-heavy, routine unclassified work such as administrative tasks, logistics, planning, and policy. Other features will be added over time.
The Pentagon positioned Grok’s capabilities and potential uses in much broader and more militaristic terms.
“Starshield AI’s Grok for Government will provide the warfighter with immediate productivity gains, stronger knowledge continuity and more secure and efficient collaboration,” according to the Defense Department’s press release. (SpaceX’s Starshield AI is a secure satellite network that uses the company’s existing Starlink tech.)
The department added that Grok would allow its military “to execute missions faster and with greater precision across numerous operational contexts, ranging from market research analysis for acquisition professionals to supply-chain management for logisticians.”
The Pentagon has struck deals with a number of other tech companies in a bid to boost its AI capabilities, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Reflection AI.

report.summary: Pentagon launches custom ChatGPT and Grok versions for 3 million personnel via secure GenAI.mil portal, boosting military AI adoption.
report.background: The U.S. Department of Defense has been integrating commercial AI tools into its workforce through GenAI.mil, a secure portal launched last year that initially offered Google Gemini. The portal is designed to give military and civilian personnel access to frontier AI models without exposing sensitive data to consumer data-collection practices. Now, custom versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok have been added, reflecting the Pentagon’s push to accelerate administrative work and military operations. Notably, Anthropic’s Claude is absent after the company refused unrestricted use and was labeled a supply-chain risk by the Trump administration—a designation Anthropic is fighting in court. The additions signal both growing acceptance of AI in defense and ongoing tensions over safety guardrails.
key_points: GenAI.mil now includes ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government alongside Google Gemini, giving 3 million Defense Department personnel access to commercial AI models in a secure, centralized environment. The portal is designed to avoid the data collection typical of consumer AI products, addressing sensitive data concerns.

Adoption has been significant: more than 1.7 million unique users—over half of the department’s personnel—have already onboarded to GenAI.mil. This shows strong demand for generative AI tools in military settings, from routine paperwork to strategic planning.

ChatGPT Mil is built through OpenAI for Government and offers a familiar ChatGPT experience, including chat, files, projects, and custom GPTs. It focuses on unclassified, document-heavy tasks such as administrative duties, logistics, planning, and policy, with more features to come.

Grok for Government is positioned in broader militaristic terms, delivered through SpaceX’s Starshield AI. The Pentagon says it will help warfighters execute missions faster and with greater precision, with applications ranging from market research for acquisition to supply-chain management for logisticians.

Anthropic’s Claude is notably absent after the company insisted on safety guardrails and was labeled a supply-chain risk by the administration. The ongoing court battle highlights the friction between AI labs’ safety commitments and the military’s desire for unrestricted tool use.
report.impact: This move normalizes the use of frontier commercial AI in military contexts, likely accelerating similar integrations across government agencies and allied forces. For the AI industry, it signals that defense contracts are lucrative but come with expectations of flexibility over safety constraints—potentially deepening divides between companies like OpenAI and xAI, which cooperate, and Anthropic, which resists. Developers may face ethical questions about building tools for warfighting, while enterprise security models may need to adapt. For regular users, the line between consumer AI and military AI blurs, raising concerns about data privacy, accountability, and how AI-driven decision-making might influence global conflicts.
report.tools: For those following developments, watch OpenAI for Government and xAI’s enterprise offerings. On the open-source side, self-hosted models like Llama 3, Mistral, and Qwen, combined with deployment tools such as Ollama and vLLM, allow secure local AI use without external data sharing. Also monitor Anthropic’s legal case and NIST’s AI risk management frameworks for guidance on ethical military AI deployment.
